title: rerank-sampling-perturbation-analysis-2026
body:
Purpose and scope

This note captures a recommended sampling and perturbation analysis protocol for reranker onboarding and ongoing regression detection. Focus: pairwise preference label collection, conversion to graded relevance, NDCG computation choices, slice-level robustness checks, and a lightweight statistical test for regressions that is practical for CI and human-in-the-loop review. It is intentionally operational — checklist + runnable sanity checks rather than pure theory.

Context / motivation

We frequently onboard new reranker models (dense or cross-encoder) and need: consistent sampling across traffic strata, robust pairwise labels that convert cleanly to graded metrics, and slice-level checks so small but important regressions (e.g., enterprise query patterns) aren't missed. Past failures: biased sampling toward short tail queries, unstable small-slice ndcg estimates, and ambiguous tie handling in annotation UI. This doc standardizes our approach and provides perturbation tests to surface sensitivity to annotation noise and model-changes.

Sampling strata and quotas (recommended)

- Global sampling overview: draw test queries from production logs for the last 30 days, deduped by normalized-query (lowercase, strip punctuation). Use stratified sampling by: query-frequency bucket, intent (informational/transactional/navigational inferred from funnel), and presence_of_entity (binary).
- Frequency buckets (approx): head (>1000/day), mid (50–1000/day), tail (1–50/day), long-tail (<1/day). Target final eval size: 5k queries minimum for basic onboarding, 20k+ for critical models.
- Per-stratum quotas (start): head 10%, mid 40%, tail 40%, long-tail 10%. Increase long-tail quota for discovery features.
- Candidate list generation: for each sampled query, produce top-K from model-under-test and one or two baseline models (K=10 recommended) to ensure reranker comparisons are meaningful. Include model-agnostic negatives (random/doc-sampled) to improve contrast.

Annotation protocol (pairwise preference)

- UI: show annotators query + two candidate results side-by-side. Provide short context: source snippet, document title, and up to 200 chars of content. Limit external clicks.
- Label schema: A>B, B>A, Tie/NoPreference, Unsure. Map labels to numeric scores for downstream graded metrics as below.
- Pair selection: sample pairs so each candidate appears in at least two different pairwise comparisons where possible (graph connectivity helps transitive inference). Prioritize pairs from different baseline models to avoid correlated errors.
- Annotator instructions highlights: judge utility for query intent, penalize hallucinated facts, prefer factual correctness over style, treat duplicates as equivalent. Provide 20-30 seed examples and a calibration quiz (>= 80% to qualify).
- IAA monitoring: compute Fleiss' kappa and Krippendorff's alpha per batch. Target kappa >= 0.45 for coarse acceptability; investigate <0.3. Keep a running disagreement log for edge cases.

Converting pairwise labels to graded relevance

We need graded relevance for NDCG. Options: direct mapping from pairwise comparisons via Bradley-Terry-like inference or deterministic heuristics when pairwise graph is sparse. Recommended pragmatic mapping:

- Build pairwise preference counts per candidate within a query. If candidate has majority wins (>60% of pairwise comparisons it participated in) -> relevance 3 (high).
- If candidate loses majority but wins >=30% -> relevance 2 (medium).
- If candidate wins <30% -> relevance 1 (low).
- If candidate is never seen or marked Unsure mostly -> relevance 0.
- Ties: count as 0.5 win for both sides when computing percentages.

Note: If you have enough pairwise data, fit a Bradley-Terry model (or TrueSkill variant) and normalize scores into 0–3 buckets for more calibrated relevance labels. Document which method used in linked_artifacts.

NDCG computation specifics

- Use DCG@k with logarithmic discount: DCG = sum_{i=1..k} (2^{rel_i}-1)/log2(i+1). NDCG = DCG / IDCG where IDCG is ideal ordering by relevance.
- Standardize on NDCG@5 and NDCG@10 for reports. Use NDCG@5 for latency-sensitive features (top results) and NDCG@10 for deeper ranking.
- When relevance buckets are derived from pairwise with ties, ensure deterministic tie-breaking for IDCG: sort candidates with equal relevance by stable doc_id to keep IDCG consistent across runs.

Perturbation analysis (robustness checks)

Run the following perturbation tests to understand metric sensitivity:

1) Annotation noise injection: flip X% of labels uniformly at random (recommended X in [2,10]). Recompute NDCG; delta should be small and symmetric. Use bootstrap to estimate 95% CI of NDCG.
2) Downsample pairs: mimic lower annotation density by subsampling pairwise graph to 50% and recompute graded conversions. Flag candidates/slices that change buckets.
3) Intent shuffling: randomly swap intent labels for 10% of queries and verify slice-ndcg stays stable.

Statistical test for regression detection (practical)

- Use block bootstrap paired test across queries: for each query compute per-query NDCG (or delta NDCG between baseline and new model). Draw bootstrap samples (10k resamples) of queries with replacement, compute distribution of mean delta. Report mean delta and two-sided bootstrap CI.
- Alert rule: if mean delta NDCG@5 < -0.01 with 95% CI entirely below 0 and p_empirical < 0.05 -> mark as potential regression. For conservative gating, use threshold -0.015.
- Small-slice adjustment: for slices with <200 queries, apply empirical Bayes shrinkage toward global mean before testing to reduce false positives.

Slice definitions and guardrails

Include both heuristic slices and signal-derived slices:

- Heuristic slices: exact-match-queries, long-queries (>6 tokens), entity-queries (contains named entity), multi-intent (contains question + commerce token), ambiguous-queries (high lexical overlap across top candidates).
- Signal-derived slices: queries with >1% CTR change historically, sessions with recent rerank fallback, frequent-query clusters from embedding-based clustering.
- Minimum slice size to report: 100 queries. For anything smaller, include in "micro-slice" list but do not auto-alert without manual review.

Example SQL snippets (pseudo)

- Sampling head queries: SELECT query, count(*) as freq FROM prod_search WHERE ts > now() - interval '30 days' GROUP BY query HAVING count(*) > 1000;
- Join candidates: use artifact table that stores model_id, ranked_list, score for reproducibility.

QA checklist before committing rollout

- Sampling reproducibility: seed and store sampling query ids and normalization steps.
- Annotation quality: IAA report + top 50 disagreement pairs saved.
- Metric compute reproducibility: store code version and convenience script that can recompute NDCG on raw pairs.
- Perturbation summary: attach sensitivity plots (noise vs delta NDCG).
- Slice review: human sign-off for any slice with delta < -0.01 or p < 0.05.

Example lightweight Python pseudocode for bootstrap test

"""
# pseudo-code (not production)
import numpy as np
def bootstrap_delta(deltas, n=10000):
    means = []
    n_q = len(deltas)
    for _ in range(n):
        sample = np.random.choice(deltas, size=n_q, replace=True)
        means.append(np.mean(sample))
    mean = np.mean(means)
    lo, hi = np.percentile(means, [2.5,97.5])
    p = (np.sum(np.array(means) <= 0) + 1) / (n + 1)  # one-sided p for no-regression hypothesis
    return mean, lo, hi, p
"""

Open questions / follow-ups

- Calibration of mapping thresholds (60/30) above — should be tuned per-product with small grid search and validated against Bradley-Terry where possible.
- Role of graded crowd labels vs expert labels for critical slices — propose hybrid: experts review top 500 disagreements.
- Consider integrating TrueSkill or BT scoring into eval pipeline for more stable relevance when pairwise graphs are dense.

Next steps (operational)

- Implement sampling SQL + reproducible artifact export (owner: Michael Chen, due: 2026-03-01).
- Add bootstrap regression test to CI for PRs that change ranking logic (owner: Asha Kapoor, due: 2026-03-15).
- Run a perturbation run on current production baseline and attach sensitivity plots to JIRA-ML-7623 (owner: Sofia Martinez).

Appendix: quick glossary

- Pairwise graph: graph where nodes = candidates, edges = annotated comparisons.
- BT: Bradley-Terry pairwise probabilistic model.
- IDCG: ideal DCG used to normalize DCG.

If you want a minimal runnable checklist/command list I can add a tiny shell + python toolset in a follow-up doc and a sample export CSV spec for pairwise labels.
